findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a Codex coordinator runs `forge land --all` for a change built by its native Codex subagent.
This condition now sends queued failures into `_handed_out`, but native work only records a pending round and prints subagent instructions (`src/forge/worker.py:290`); it does not execute the repair. `_handed_out` consequently returns true, and land exits successfully at line 130 before closing again. The queue treats that successful exit as a completed merge (`src/forge/land.py:411`), reporting the still-failing, unmerged change as merged. It requires handback and another land invocation to finish. Keep native repairs pending through handback and the subsequent close instead of counting the handoff as a merge. The new regression test exercises only Claude SDK workers, so it misses this path.

why: When CI fails on a change in a batch run, the run stops that change and the owner has to start its fix round again by hand, while a single change gets that round itself.
